title: Light Well Shaft Reflectance Simulator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates a vertical light well shaft commonly found in dense urban architecture. The simulator lets users configure shaft geometry, wall materials, and a sky/sun light source, then visualizes how light bounces and attenuates down the shaft using a simplified ray-bounce reflectance model.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera starting at position (0, 15, 25) looking toward the origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- A ground plane at y=0 (dark gray, 20x20).
- The light well is a rectangular vertical shaft centered at the origin. Default dimensions: width=4, depth=4, height=20 (meters). The shaft is open at the top and bottom sits on the ground plane.
- Render the shaft walls as four separate BoxGeometry slabs (front, back, left, right) so each wall is individually addressable. Default wall color: #C8B8A0 (sandstone). Use MeshStandardMaterial.
- Place a DirectionalLight at (5, 40, 5) intensity 1.5 simulating the sun, plus ambient light intensity 0.3.
- Add a small yellow sphere (radius 0.3) at the top-center of the shaft representing the light entry point.

## Reflectance Model
- Implement a simplified reflectance simulation: divide the shaft into 10 vertical zones (slices) from top to bottom. Each zone has a computed illuminance value (0.0 to 1.0).
- The top zone starts at illuminance = 1.0. Each subsequent zone's illuminance = previous_zone * wallReflectance * geometryFactor.
- wallReflectance is a material property (default 0.55 for sandstone). geometryFactor = min(1.0, (width * depth) / (height_per_zone * 2.0)), representing how shaft aspect ratio affects light propagation.
- Visualize illuminance by tinting each zone of the shaft walls: brighter zones are closer to the wall base color, darker zones blend toward black. Apply this as vertex colors or by splitting wall geometry into 10 vertical segments with per-segment emissive values.
- Also place 10 small flat planes (0.3x0.3) on the back wall at the center of each zone as "sensor patches" colored from bright yellow (high illuminance) to dark blue (low illuminance) using a heatmap gradient.

## UI Controls (DOM overlay, top-left panel)
- "Shaft Width" slider: range 2-8, step 0.5, default 4. Changes shaft width in real time.
- "Shaft Height" slider: range 10-40, step 1, default 20. Changes shaft height.
- "Wall Reflectance" slider: range 0.1-0.95, step 0.05, default 0.55.
- "Wall Material" dropdown: 'Sandstone' (reflectance 0.55, color #C8B8A0), 'White Paint' (reflectance 0.85, color #F0F0F0), 'Concrete' (reflectance 0.35, color #808080), 'Dark Brick' (reflectance 0.20, color #6B3A2A).
- "Run Simulation" button: recalculates all zone illuminances and updates visuals.
- "Export Data" button: logs the 10 zone illuminance values to console and stores them in state.
- Display a HUD text element showing: "Bottom Illuminance: X.XXXX" (the illuminance of the lowest zone).

## Keyboard Interactions
- Press 'R' to reset all parameters to defaults and re-run simulation.
- Press 'T' to toggle a translucent top-cover on the shaft (a semi-transparent plane at the top, which multiplies all illuminances by 0.7 when active). Toggle state tracked.
- Press '1'-'4' to quick-select wall materials (1=Sandstone, 2=White Paint, 3=Concrete, 4=Dark Brick) and auto-run simulation.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- shaftWidth: number (current width)
- shaftHeight: number (current height)
- shaftDepth: number (always equals shaftWidth for square shaft)
- wallReflectance: number (current reflectance)
- wallMaterial: string ('Sandstone'|'White Paint'|'Concrete'|'Dark Brick')
- wallColor: string (hex color of current material)
- zoneIlluminances: array of 10 numbers (top to bottom)
- bottomIlluminance: number (last zone value)
- topCoverActive: boolean
- geometryFactor: number (current computed geometry factor)
- simulationRunCount: number (increments each time simulation runs)
- sensorPatchCount: number (should be 10)
- zonesAboveThreshold: number (count of zones with illuminance > 0.1)
- totalLightSum: number (sum of all 10 zone illuminances)
- dataExported: boolean (true after Export Data clicked)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z}

Run the simulation once automatically on page load so initial state is populated.
physics_constraints: Light illuminance must monotonically decrease from top zone to bottom zone. Each zone illuminance = previous * wallReflectance * geometryFactor, clamped [0,1]. geometryFactor = min(1.0, (width*depth)/(zoneHeight*2.0)). When top cover is active, all illuminances are multiplied by 0.7. Total light sum must equal the mathematical geometric series sum within floating point tolerance. No NaN or negative illuminance values permitted.
